goal: Explain how a custom WPF title bar can preserve the Windows 11 Snap Layout hover affordance or provide the closest supported workaround.
must_include: Explains that Snap Layouts are tied to the OS-recognized non-client maximize button/hit-test behavior, not merely any WPF button that toggles `WindowState`.
Recommends preserving or exposing a real caption/maximize hit-test area, such as using `WindowChrome` hit-test behavior carefully or leaving the native caption button in place.
If using the XAML-only workaround, describes leaving a transparent/no-fill hit-test hole or region so hover can reach the WindowChrome/non-client maximize area while keeping custom visuals around it.
Mentions Win+Z as a fallback for users, but not as a full replacement for fixing the hover affordance.
must_not: Claim Snap Layouts can be shown by calling a public WPF API from the custom button click handler.
Suggest simulating the Windows 11 Snap Layout flyout with a custom menu as an equivalent OS integration.
Remove resize/drag support from the custom title bar to solve the maximize hover issue.
acceptable_alternatives: Use the native title bar/caption buttons and customize only allowed title-bar content.
Use a Win32 non-client hit-test implementation for the maximize button area if the app already owns its HWND message handling.
solved: The answer ties Snap Layouts to native caption hit testing and gives a concrete WPF WindowChrome/native-titlebar approach that preserves the OS hover behavior.
partial: The answer says the custom button blocks Snap Layouts but only offers Win+Z or a custom menu without a real title-bar integration path.
notes: The Stack Overflow answer describes an imperfect XAML-only workaround and links to broader WPF discussion; robust apps may prefer native caption preservation or explicit HWND hit testing.
